That listener uses the pre-local-substitution payload damage and selected tier health/time. Local idamage=1, self.health++ and self.laststanddamage follow notification; they do not explicitly rewrite params. The later damage gate can return after these side effects. Revive marker/clears and cancellation paths are mapped without claiming listener ordering, native delivery, parameter alias rules or real PS4 behavior.

summary.answer: The saved damage and return value belong to the actual final-damage receiver. A normal return from finishplayerdamage supplies an initial fatal value; after the optional status helper the source re-reads laststand. If laststand is true it replaces that value with either the installed pointer result (and then clears saved damage) or literal1 when either required field is absent. The three final-damage callsites include a reflected friendly-fire call on the attacker: a second result can overwrite the first victim result. The outer callback passes its resulting fatal variable into damage feedback; the shown override/feedback code does not itself call the native downing or killing operation. Actual native damage/death effects already lie across finishplayerdamage and remain unknown.
